title: Location Data Identifies Child's Movements
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from child's device can be used to identify the child's precise location, movements, and patterns of behavior, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities, school, home, and social interactions.

title: GPS Data Linkable to Other Information
description: GPS coordinates can be linked with other data sources (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and associations, enabling tracking across different contexts and time periods.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted to the backend may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls, exposing the child's real-time location to malicious actors.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Continuous live GPS tracking at regular intervals may collect more location data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles and potentially exposing the child to unnecessary privacy risks.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Children's Data
description: Collection and processing of children's location data may violate GDPR, COPPA, and other child privacy regulations that impose stricter requirements for consent, data protection, and parental oversight.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties without proper access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Access controls on DS1 are insufficient or compromised

title: Location Data Tampering
description: Location data in DS1 could be modified or deleted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially enabling false location claims.
assumptions: DS1 lacks adequate integrity controls

title: Individual Identification via Location Data
description: Location history data could directly identify individuals through patterns of movement, home/work locations, and frequent visitation patterns.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals

title: Cross-System Data Linking
description: Location data in DS1 could be linked with other data sources (e.g., device IDs, user accounts) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other identifiers

title: Inappropriate Data Retention
description: Backend process P1 may retain location data longer than necessary, increasing exposure risk and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Retention policies are not properly enforced

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Location data collection and storage may not comply with GDPR or other privacy regulations regarding consent, purpose limitation, and data subject rights.
assumptions: Privacy compliance measures are inadequate

title: Location Data Identifies Individual

assumptions: Location data is transmitted without sufficient anonymization or aggregation

title: Location Data Linkable Across Sessions
description: Location pings from the Mobile App Backend can be linked across multiple sessions and time periods, enabling the creation of detailed movement profiles that track user behavior over time.
assumptions: Location data is stored and accessible across different processing sessions

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine may collect and process more location data than necessary for zone entry/exit detection, including historical location data or data beyond the geofencing purpose.

title: Non-Compliance with Location Privacy Regulations
description: The geofencing system may fail to comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding location data processing, including lack of user consent, transparency, or data subject rights.
assumptions: The system does not implement proper consent mechanisms or regulatory compliance measures

title: Linkability of Zone Definitions to Individuals
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in DS2 could be linked to specific family members, revealing their locations, routines, and relationships. This linkage could enable profiling or tracking of individuals through their configured geofencing zones.
assumptions: Zone definitions are associated with specific family members or user accounts

title: Identifiability Through Location Data
description: The zone definitions in DS2 could be used to identify specific individuals or their physical locations. Knowledge of home, school, and friend's house locations could reveal personal information about family members.
assumptions: Zone definitions are not sufficiently anonymized or obfuscated

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Preferences
description: Zone definitions containing sensitive location information (home, school, friend's house) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls in DS2.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or encryption for sensitive location data

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) may collect and process more location-related data than necessary for the intended geofencing functionality, potentially including precise coordinates or movement patterns beyond what's needed for zone-based alerts.
assumptions: System collects more granular location data than required for basic geofencing

title: Usurpation of Geofencing Permissions
description: Unauthorized actors could potentially exploit the geofencing permissions in P2 to impersonate family members or gain unauthorized access to location-based services, potentially leading to stalking or surveillance.
assumptions: Authentication and authorization mechanisms in P2 are vulnerable to exploitation

title: Linkability of Movement Patterns
description: The geofencing notification could be linked to specific individuals based on their movement patterns across multiple zones, enabling tracking of a child's location history over time.
assumptions: Notifications contain sufficient identifying information to link to specific children; multiple zone entries/exits are recorded.

title: Identification of Zone Entry/Exit
description: Unauthorized parties could identify which specific child entered or exited a geofenced zone based on the notification content.
assumptions: Notification contains child identifiers or can be correlated with known individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location-based notifications could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the parent entity.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not adequately secured; notification data is not properly encrypted.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The system may collect more location data than necessary for the stated purpose of geofencing alerts, potentially including unnecessary zone details or timestamps.
assumptions: Data collection exceeds minimum requirements for the geofencing functionality.

title: Unauthorized Data Leakage of Family Account Information
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could leak sensitive family account credentials, child profile data, and geofence zone information to unauthorized third parties through vulnerabilities in the backend system or insecure data transmission channels.
assumptions: Assumes backend has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile and Geofence Data
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could allow unauthorized actors to modify child profile information or geofence zone settings, potentially leading to false location tracking or altered parental controls.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient authentication and authorization controls on the backend

title: Identification of Children Through Profile and Location Data
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) could enable identification of individual children through their stored profiles, geofence patterns, and associated family account information, potentially exposing minors' identities.
assumptions: Assumes data is accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Unintended Consequences from Geofence Data Collection
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could create unintended consequences by collecting and storing geofence zone data that reveals family routines, schedules, and locations, potentially enabling stalking or unwanted surveillance.
assumptions: Assumes geofence data is retained longer than necessary and not properly anonymized

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location data
description: The mobile app backend may disclose the child's current location or location history to unauthorized parties, including third-party services, advertisers, or malicious actors who gain access to the system.

title: Identification through location patterns
description: Location data can reveal sensitive information about the child's daily routines, home address, school, workplace, and frequent locations, potentially enabling identification of the child's identity and personal habits.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The system may collect location data beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose of viewing location on a map, potentially storing historical data that exceeds the minimum required for the parent's request.

title: Unauthorized access to child's location
description: Unauthorized users or systems may gain access to the child's location data without proper authentication or authorization controls, potentially through vulnerabilities in the mobile app backend.

title: Linkability of location data with other personal information
description: The child's location data may be linked with other personal information (e.g., name, age, school, family information) to create a comprehensive profile that could be used for tracking or profiling purposes.

title: Location History Linkability
description: Stored location history can be linked to other data sources (e.g., device IDs, timestamps, user profiles) to create comprehensive movement profiles that reveal patterns of life, habits, and associations.
assumptions: Location data is stored with sufficient granularity and temporal resolution to enable meaningful linkage with other datasets.

title: Location History Identifiability
description: Location history patterns (e.g., home/work addresses, frequent routes) can be used to identify specific individuals even without explicit identifiers, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Location data contains unique patterns or landmarks that can be correlated with known personal information.

title: Unauthorized Location History Disclosure
description: Location history data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security breaches, improper access controls, or insider threats, exposing sensitive movement patterns.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed; data is transmitted or stored without adequate encryption.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The backend may collect and store more location history data than necessary for serving the map/history view, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system retains historical location data beyond what is needed for the stated purpose, or collects location data at higher granularity than required.

title: Location History Access Usurpation
description: Unauthorized users could gain access to another user's location history through weak authentication, session hijacking, or account takeover.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust; session management has vulnerabilities.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing location history data may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, transparency, and data subject rights are not implemented.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations; consent mechanisms are inadequate.

title: Linkability of Parent Identity to Child Location
description: The parent's identity (EE1) is linked to the child's location data through the invitation process, creating a traceable connection between the guardian and the child's whereabouts.
assumptions: The system logs which parent initiated the secondary guardian invitation.

title: Identifiability of Child Through Location Data
description: The secondary guardian can identify the child's identity and routine patterns through access to location data, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's daily activities.
assumptions: Location data includes timestamps and geographic coordinates that can be correlated with known locations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Location
description: The secondary guardian may share or leak the child's location information with unauthorized third parties, leading to potential stalking or unwanted surveillance.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has no technical or legal restrictions preventing them from sharing the data.

title: Usurpation of Parent Identity
description: An unauthorized person could impersonate the parent (EE1) to invite a secondary guardian, gaining access to the child's location data without legitimate authority.
assumptions: The invitation process lacks robust authentication mechanisms to verify the parent's identity.

title: Excessive Location Data Sharing
description: The system may share more location data than necessary (e.g., historical data, precise coordinates) with the secondary guardian, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The data sharing policy does not enforce strict data minimization for secondary guardian access.

title: Non-compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: Sharing child location data with secondary guardians may violate child privacy laws (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) if proper consent mechanisms and age-appropriate safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: The system does not have adequate consent management and legal compliance features for child data sharing.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's live location to secondary guardian
description: The backend process shares the child's live location with the secondary guardian without proper verification of authorization or consent, potentially exposing sensitive personal data to unauthorized recipients.

title: Interception of location data in transit
description: The child's live location data transmitted from the backend to the secondary guardian could be intercepted by malicious actors during transmission, leading to unauthorized access to real-time location information.

title: Linkability of location data to child's identity
description: The shared location data can be linked to the child's identity, enabling tracking of the child's movements and potentially revealing patterns of behavior, school attendance, or home location.

title: Unawareness of data sharing scope
description: Parents or the child may not be fully aware of the extent of location data being shared with the secondary guardian, including duration, frequency, and specific data points transmitted.

title: Secondary guardian misuses location data
description: The secondary guardian may misuse the child's location data beyond the intended purpose, such as sharing it with third parties, storing it longer than necessary, or using it for unauthorized surveillance.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Analytics Partner
description: The backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an advertising/analytics partner, which may include more data than necessary for the stated purpose of funding the app's free tier.
assumptions: The analytics partner may have access to detailed user behavior data that exceeds what's needed for basic analytics.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Even though data is described as 'aggregated', patterns in usage and engagement analytics could potentially be linked back to specific users through cross-referencing with other data sources or advanced analytics techniques.
assumptions: The advertising partner may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with the shared analytics to re-identify users.

title: Unauthorized Data Usage by Analytics Partner
description: The advertising/analytics partner may use the shared usage and engagement analytics for purposes beyond the agreed scope (e.g., building user profiles, selling data to third parties, or targeting users in ways not consented to).
assumptions: The partner may not be fully bound by privacy agreements or may have incentives to exploit the data beyond the stated purpose.

title: Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The advertising/analytics partner may disclose the received analytics data to additional third parties (e.g., data brokers, advertisers, or other partners) without proper authorization or user consent.
assumptions: The partner may have business relationships or contractual obligations that require sharing data with other entities.

title: Location data reveals child's precise whereabouts
description: The child's current location data in the SOS/check-in message can identify their precise physical location, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routine, school, home, or other activities.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: The child's location information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls on the Mobile App Backend.

title: Location data linkability with other data sources
description: The location data could be linked with other data about the child (e.g., school records, medical information, social media activity) to create a comprehensive profile that reveals more than intended.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The Mobile App Backend may collect and retain location data beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose of sending check-in/SOS messages to the parent, violating data minimization principles.

title: Potential GDPR compliance issues
description: The processing of children's location data may raise compliance concerns under GDPR and other data protection regulations, particularly regarding consent, data retention, and purpose limitation.
